- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates — apply downward bias of 2–5% to forecasted mean.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model often lags — delay upward correction by 1–2 periods.
- If forecast mean is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive periods, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% from next forecast if sentiment remains neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate volatility — smooth forecast curve by reducing standard deviation by 15–20% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
